The Berrios factor structure is the governing frame: Cotard's syndrome cuts across diagnostic categories (psychotic-depression factor, pure type I closer to delusional disorders, mixed type II), so the depressive-disorder edge records embedding within a syndrome population, not causation; the reverse reading (severe depression generating the syndrome) is equally documented and is recorded in the guard.
governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: the 100-case series and the 2005-2018 case-review both document major depression in the large majority of Cotard presentations (89%; psychotic-depression the leading factor), but the syndrome is explicitly a cross-cutting presentation with a pure non-affective form, so neither direction is asserted.

Bidirectionality/identity guard recorded: Cotard's syndrome is not in ICD-10 or DSM-5 and is best modeled as a delusional presentation occurring within psychotic depression, other psychoses, or organic disease; an edge in either direction risks restating the diagnostic picture (the ME-41 barrier noted for other syndrome identities), so the edge records documented co-occurrence only, mirroring the capgras-syndrome precedent.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The analysis of 100 historical and modern cases found depression reported in 89% of subjects, with exploratory factor analysis extracting psychotic-depression, Cotard type I (no depression loadings, closer to delusional disorders), and mixed type II factors, concluding the syndrome cuts across diagnostic categories (Berrios 1995); the systematic review of 69 reported cases from 2005-2018 found major depression significantly more frequent in older patients and extracted the same psychotic-depression factor leading the structure (Huarcaya-Victoria 2020); the case report and review situates Cotard's within psychotic depression with ECT as the most reported successful treatment and records associated organic conditions (Moschopoulos 2016).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the co-occurrence is better modeled as embedding of the syndrome within severe depressive episodes (or within non-affective psychosis and organic disease in other cases), the pure type I form shows no depression loadings, and reverse generation (depressive illness producing the syndrome) is the standard clinical reading, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A shared-severity pathway is hypothesized: nihilistic delusions arise within the most severe depressive episodes as psychotic elaborations of mood-congruent negation (guilt, damnation, bodily nonexistence), while in the pure form the same delusions occur without affective illness; shared dopaminergic-limbic and self-referential-processing disturbances are the proposed substrate for both. Both directions are biologically coherent and documented, but the syndrome's cross-cutting factor structure defeats a single directional arrow, so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Depressive disorder co-occurs with Cotard's syndrome in the large majority of documented cases as part of the syndrome's psychotic-depression factor; individual determination requires psychiatric diagnostic documentation of the depressive episode and the delusional content with chronology, exclusion of organic and substance causes, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Structured psychiatric diagnostic evaluation documenting the depressive episode (duration, severity, melancholic and psychotic features) and the nihilistic delusional content with chronology; neuromedical workup excluding organic etiologies (infarction, encephalitis, tumor, epilepsy, traumatic brain injury) and substance-induced psychosis; treatment-response documentation; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pure Cotard type I without affective illness (delusional-disorder proximity)
Organic etiologies (cerebral infarction, encephalitis, tumor, epilepsy, traumatic brain injury)
Postpartum and catatonic presentations without primary depression

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the co-occurrence is the best-documented fact in the syndrome's literature (89% depression; psychotic-depression the leading factor), but the syndrome's cross-cutting structure and the standard reverse reading defeat any causal arrow; the edge records documented co-occurrence only, mirroring the capgras-syndrome precedent.
